/blog/guides/faceless-youtube-channel-10.blocks.7.items.3: **Digital product** — template pack, notion system, or mini-course; $1K and pure margin.
/blog/guides/faceless-youtube-channel-10.blocks.8.text: That stack is $10K at roughly 1.5M monthly views — a fraction of the views AdSense-only would demand. Build affiliate links in from video one; sponsors come to channels that look like businesses.
/blog/guides/faceless-youtube-channel-10.blocks.10.items.0: Days 1–14: build the system, bank six videos before publishing anything.
/blog/guides/faceless-youtube-channel-10.blocks.10.items.1: Days 15–45: publish 3/week. Double down on the two videos with retention above 40%; kill formats below 25%.
/blog/guides/faceless-youtube-channel-10.blocks.10.items.2: Days 46–90: add a Shorts funnel cut from winners, assemble a media kit, pitch five sponsors with your retention data.
/blog/guides/faceless-youtube-channel-10.blocks.12.items.0: Format drift — chasing trends until the channel has no identity.
/blog/guides/faceless-youtube-channel-10.blocks.12.items.1: Cadence collapse — the algorithm forgives a slow week, not a silent month.
/blog/guides/faceless-youtube-channel-10.blocks.12.items.2: Raw unedited AI slop — viewers and the algorithm both punish generation that was not edited with intent.
/blog/guides/faceless-youtube-channel-10.blocks.12.items.3: Ignoring retention graphs — the graph tells you exactly which 30 seconds to fix.
/blog/guides/faceless-youtube-channel-10.blocks.13.title: Consistency compounds
/blog/guides/faceless-youtube-channel-10.blocks.13.body: Channels that survive 90 days of cadence usually cross monetization. The failure point is system collapse, not idea shortage — which is why the consistency discipline from our persona guides matters as much here as in advertising.
/blog/guides/faceless-youtube-channel-10.blocks.14.text: Companion piece: our blog's faceless-channel starter guide covers the platform setup; this guide covers the machine that makes it pay.

/blog/guides/recreate-39500-month-facele.title: Recreate a $39,500/Month Faceless Channel: The Teardown Method
/blog/guides/recreate-39500-month-facele.excerpt: You do not clone videos — you clone systems. How to reverse-engineer any working channel into a production spec, validate it in 30 days, then automate what is proven.
/blog/guides/recreate-39500-month-facele.blocks.0.text: Somewhere in your niche is a faceless channel printing money with a format you could run. The move is not to steal its videos — that gets channels nuked and sponsors spooked. The move is to tear it down into a production spec and rebuild the system with your own topics, your own voice, your own visuals. Here is the teardown method.
/blog/guides/recreate-39500-month-facele.blocks.2.text: One row per channel, five channels. Columns:
/blog/guides/recreate-39500-month-facele.blocks.3.items.1: Cadence — uploads per week, consistency streak.
/blog/guides/recreate-39500-month-facele.blocks.3.items.2: Hook patterns — first five seconds of their top 20 videos, written out.
/blog/guides/recreate-39500-month-facele.blocks.3.items.3: Retention device — what happens at 30-second intervals to hold you.
/blog/guides/recreate-39500-month-facele.blocks.3.items.4: Visual style — grade, shot types, motion density.
/blog/guides/recreate-39500-month-facele.blocks.3.items.5: Monetization — ads, affiliates, sponsors, products; check descriptions and pinned comments.
/blog/guides/recreate-39500-month-facele.blocks.3.items.6: Outlier signal — views divided by the channel's median. Outliers reveal what the audience wants more of.
/blog/guides/recreate-39500-month-facele.blocks.5.text: Documentary-style history channel, 12-minute videos, three per week, $7 RPM, 1.7M monthly views. Revenue: $12K AdSense, $15K sponsors (two reads a week at this scale), $8K affiliates (books, courses, documentaries), $4.5K own product. Total: $39.5K. Note what the math says: AdSense is under a third of the money. Anyone copying "the channel" while copying only its ads revenue is copying a third of the business.
/blog/guides/recreate-39500-month-facele.blocks.7.items.0: Topic research agent — finds outliers across your five channels: views ÷ median > 5 becomes a candidate brief.
/blog/guides/recreate-39500-month-facele.blocks.7.items.1: Script agent — runs the format bible from your teardown: hook patterns, chapter rhythm, payoff placement.
/blog/guides/recreate-39500-month-facele.blocks.7.items.2: Visual pipeline — style bible plus the video generators; consistency rules from the continuity guide keep 40+ b-roll shots per video coherent.
/blog/guides/recreate-39500-month-facele.blocks.7.items.3: Edit checklist — cut rhythm, pattern interrupts, caption pass.
/blog/guides/recreate-39500-month-facele.blocks.7.items.4: Packaging agent — three title and thumbnail variants per video; you pick, it never auto-publishes.
/blog/guides/recreate-39500-month-facele.blocks.7.items.5: Human QA gates — script approval and final cut. Everything else runs without you.
/blog/guides/recreate-39500-month-facele.blocks.9.text: Run eight videos with the pipeline half-manual before you automate anything. You are looking for format-market fit: retention above 40%, CTR above 4%, at least one outlier. Automating an unproven format does not save time — it manufactures waste at machine speed.
/blog/guides/recreate-39500-month-facele.blocks.10.title: Copy the economics, not the videos
/blog/guides/recreate-39500-month-facele.blocks.10.body: Same niche, same format, different topics, your own voice and visuals. Never re-upload or paraphrase-and-paste; platforms detect duplicates and audiences detect provenance. The teardown is a spec, not a source.
/blog/guides/recreate-39500-month-facele.blocks.12.text: The old moat was edit throughput — hours of b-roll sourcing and timeline work per video. Generation collapses that cost to near zero, which moves the moat to taste, topic selection, and QA. Your edge is the consistency systems and agent direction this site teaches, applied to a format someone else already validated with their audience.
/blog/guides/recreate-39500-month-facele.blocks.13.text: When the system runs, the ceiling is portfolio, not hours: the same teardown sheet, run again in the adjacent niche, is channel two.

/blog/guides/automated-ai-business.title: How to Build an Automated AI Business
/blog/guides/automated-ai-business.excerpt: The real automation opportunity: productized offers where agents run production and humans run sales and QA. The pipeline pattern, the math, and the build order that avoids the classic corpse.
/blog/guides/automated-ai-business.blocks.0.text: "Automated AI business" usually means a dashboard selling a course about a dashboard. The real version is unglamorous and profitable: a productized offer — fixed scope, fixed price — where agents handle production and humans handle judgment. Six clients at $2K a month is a real business with 70–85% margins. Here is the operating manual.
/blog/guides/automated-ai-business.blocks.2.text: One offer: "30 ad creatives a month, $2K", "one faceless video channel run for you, $3K", "50 product photos per season, $1.5K". Fixed scope forces you to learn what the work actually is. Agents multiply clarity and fog equally — handing an agent a vague offer gives you vague output at machine speed.
/blog/guides/automated-ai-business.blocks.4.items.0: Intake form — the client answers twenty questions once. This is your brief generator's input.
/blog/guides/automated-ai-business.blocks.4.items.1: Brief generator — converts intake into the production brief: deliverable list, acceptance criteria, references attached.
/blog/guides/automated-ai-business.blocks.4.items.2: Agent production line — parallel where items are independent, ordered where dependent. The directing-agents guide is the manual.
/blog/guides/automated-ai-business.blocks.4.items.3: Human QA gates — judgment points where a person approves against the sheet: script pass, brand pass, final pass.
/blog/guides/automated-ai-business.blocks.4.items.4: Delivery plus report — what shipped, what won, what mutates next cycle. The report is the retention engine.
/blog/guides/automated-ai-business.blocks.5.text: What agents run well vs badly
/blog/guides/automated-ai-business.blocks.6.items.0: Good: variant generation, first-pass scripts, asset organization, format conversion, reporting, the boring 80%.
/blog/guides/automated-ai-business.blocks.6.items.1: Bad: taste calls, brand judgment, client politics, final approval, pricing conversations.
/blog/guides/automated-ai-business.blocks.6.items.2: Design consequence: every pipeline terminates at a human gate. Agents hand to people at judgment points, never past them.
/blog/guides/automated-ai-business.blocks.8.text: Six clients at $2K = $12K monthly. Production compute runs $100–300 across the book of business. Your time: sales plus one to two QA hours per client per week. That is the whole model — the margin is real because generation collapsed production cost, and the risk is real because churn eats everything. Weekly reports with winner analysis are what keep clients into month four, where the business actually lives.
/blog/guides/automated-ai-business.blocks.10.items.0: Deliver the offer manually to two or three clients. Feel where the hours go.
/blog/guides/automated-ai-business.blocks.10.items.1: Write the brief template from what you repeated three times.
/blog/guides/automated-ai-business.blocks.10.items.2: Automate one node at a time — the one-variable discipline from the ComfyUI guide applies to business systems too.
/blog/guides/automated-ai-business.blocks.10.items.3: Only automate what you have done manually ten times. Everything else stays human until it is boring.
/blog/guides/automated-ai-business.blocks.11.title: Automate version two, not version one
/blog/guides/automated-ai-business.blocks.11.body: Premature automation of an unvalidated offer is the number-one killer in this category. Validation is manual; automation is what you earn by validating.
/blog/guides/automated-ai-business.blocks.13.items.0: Proprietary asset libraries — Soul ID sheets, style bibles, scene plates tuned per client.
/blog/guides/automated-ai-business.blocks.13.items.1: Winner data loops — you know which of the client's creatives converted; the next agency starts blind.
/blog/guides/automated-ai-business.blocks.13.items.2: Iteration speed — your kill-and-mutate cycle runs in days, theirs runs in weeks.
/blog/guides/automated-ai-business.blocks.13.items.3: Never the model. Everyone has the model.

/blog/guides/ecommerce-product-photos-wi.title: E-commerce Product Photos Without a Studio
/blog/guides/ecommerce-product-photos-wi.excerpt: Catalogs need constant imagery; studios charge $30–100 a shot and book out weeks. The AI pipeline: capture the source right, build scene plates once, batch by collection, sell per-SKU packages.
/blog/guides/ecommerce-product-photos-wi.blocks.0.text: Every e-commerce brand has the same recurring bill: product photography. New SKUs, seasonal refreshes, marketplace requirements — at $30–100+ per shot and multi-week lead times, a 100-SKU catalog spends five figures a year staying current. The AI pipeline produces scene-consistent product sets in hours. The product pixels stay real; only the world around them is generated.
/blog/guides/ecommerce-product-photos-wi.blocks.2.items.0: Phone on a white foam-board sweep, window light, no flash.
/blog/guides/ecommerce-product-photos-wi.blocks.2.items.1: Three angles per SKU: hero front, 45-degree, one macro detail of texture or mechanism.
/blog/guides/ecommerce-product-photos-wi.blocks.2.items.2: Wipe fingerprints and dust first — generation faithfully reproduces smudges too.
/blog/guides/ecommerce-product-photos-wi.blocks.2.items.3: Same distance and height per SKU so the batch composites consistently.
/blog/guides/ecommerce-product-photos-wi.blocks.3.text: Ten minutes per product, once. This is the entire studio cost of the pipeline.
/blog/guides/ecommerce-product-photos-wi.blocks.5.text: Generate a library of scene plates for the brand's world: marble kitchen counter, spa bathroom, wooden desk flat-lay, gym bench, outdoor patio at golden hour. Each plate gets a light signature — direction, quality, color — exactly like location plates in the continuity guide. New product shots are reference edits compositing the source photo into a plate, then relit to match the plate's light. The scene library is the asset that compounds; every new SKU gets cheaper.
/blog/guides/ecommerce-product-photos-wi.blocks.6.text: Batch by collection, not by SKU
/blog/guides/ecommerce-product-photos-wi.blocks.7.text: Run the whole spring line in one session: same scene, same light, same grade. Catalog pages where every product sits in the same world read as a professional brand; a mix of lighting per SKU reads as a garage sale no matter how good each image is. Consistency across the grid sells harder than fidelity in any single frame.
/blog/guides/ecommerce-product-photos-wi.blocks.9.items.0: Amazon main image — pure white background, product fills 85% of frame, no props, no text, no logos other than the product's.
/blog/guides/ecommerce-product-photos-wi.blocks.9.items.1: Lifestyle variants — the scene-plate composites, for A+ content and social.
/blog/guides/ecommerce-product-photos-wi.blocks.9.items.2: Shopify grids — 1:1 crops, consistent padding per collection.
/blog/guides/ecommerce-product-photos-wi.blocks.9.items.3: Zoom-ready — upscale final selects to 2000px+ so fabric texture survives inspection.
/blog/guides/ecommerce-product-photos-wi.blocks.9.items.4: File naming — SKU, angle, scene. Catalog managers will love you and rehire you.
/blog/guides/ecommerce-product-photos-wi.blocks.11.text: Sell per-SKU packages: five to eight images (white-background set plus three to five scene composites) at $15–40 per SKU, against the studio's $150+ equivalent. Target brands with 50+ SKUs where studio cost is an annual argument. Position it as catalog refresh and conversion work, never as "AI images" — the buyer is buying a current catalog, not a technology.
/blog/guides/ecommerce-product-photos-wi.blocks.12.title: Product truth is non-negotiable
/blog/guides/ecommerce-product-photos-wi.blocks.12.body: Never let generation invent features, change proportions, or restyle the product itself. The source photo defines the product; generation builds only the world around it. Customers return products that do not match their photos — and brands fire vendors whose photos cause returns.
/blog/guides/ecommerce-product-photos-wi.blocks.14.text: The same plates and sources produce five to ten second product motion loops for product pages and social — slow orbit, pour, steam, texture rack focus — via the video generators. Price the video set at two to three times the photo package; it is the same session's assets doing double duty.
